thread:
sara: Heads up — after last night's driver roll (535 -> 550) a subset of us-west2 GPU nodes are failing to finish provisioning. Observed during canary -> staggered rollout. :frowning:

matt: Seen similar on two nodes. DKMS rebuild errors + modprobe uvm fails. I have an OOB node with logs.

matt: paste:
```
DKMS: build error
ERROR: Could not insert 'nvidia': Unknown symbol in module
nvidia_uvm: Unknown symbol __x86_indirect_thunk_r13
```

jen: Kernel version on effected nodes?

sara: 5.15.0-1033-aws on most, some auto-upgraded to 5.19 in a handful of hosts (weird mix from baseline image drift).

dinesh: That thunk symbol usually means module compiled against different GCC/IPP/CONFIG (clang vs gcc?) or CONFIG_RETPOLINE mismatch — DKMS rebuilt against running headers might not match.

kevin: Are these all on the nvlink-enabled instances? We saw p2p errors in NVLINK tests earlier.

matt: Yes, p4d and a100-80 nodes. Also seeing nccl tests failing with peer errors: "rank 0 P2P connect failed".

infra-bot: deploy-bot initiated rollout step: canary group -> 15% -> 40% (paused).

jen: What's the % of capacity impact?

sara: us-west2 GPU pool: ~12% of GPUs are currently out of rotation while we triage. Queue times for infer/rl batches up ~30% per job. Cost impact is visible because we had to burst to AWS spot fleets for short term.

dinesh: Quick repro: when headers mismatch DKMS still 'succeeds' but module has unresolved symbols. Suggest puling kernel-headers from the image that matches the running kernel and rebuild. Also check /usr/src/nvidia-*/build/make.log for exact compiler flags.

matt: Tried rebuild on one host: `dkms remove -m nvidia -v 550 --all && dkms add -m nvidia -v 550 && dkms build -m nvidia -v 550 && dkms install -m nvidia -v 550` -> build passes but modprobe still errors. The installed ko shows different vermagic.

kevin: Vermagic mismatch indicates installed module was built for a different kernel release. That explains Unknown symbol. How are images being provisioned? Cloud-init hooks?

sara: Provisioner uses pre-baked AMI with headers package baked in. Some hosts got drifted by unattended-upgrades pulling newer kernels (we forgot to pin linux-image).

jen: Can we patch the DKMS hook to force rebuild against current running kernel and fail early (so node doesn't join pool until module usable)?

dinesh: Yes — add an early check in the onboarding script: verify `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic` equals `uname -r`. If mismatch then stop and report to infra. Also, switch off unattended-upgrades for kernel packages in AMI.

matt: Temporary mitigation: roll back driver to 535 on a small set and re-run staging tests. That recovered two nodes. But rollback reduces perf for some workloads (higher token latency on some models) so not ideal long term.

kevin: Also observed NVLINK fabric flapping when mixed kernel versions in same rack. NCCL channels degrade. Might be safest to drain racks with mixed kernels until images are uniform.

infra-bot: action: tagged affected hosts and removed from LB.

jen: Who can lead the rollback/coordination? We need to weigh risk vs cost (degraded perf) vs time to fix image.

sara: I'm coordinating rollback for the remaining 20 canaries, matt + dinesh are triaging DKMS script fix, kevin will test NCCl p2p across racks once nodes stabilized.

matt: Planning steps: 1) Pause rollout 2) Pin unattended-upgrades for kernel packages in AMI 3) Add vermagic check in onboarding 4) Rolling rollback to 535 for affected nodes 5) Full run of NCCL p2p tests + perf regression benchmarks.

dinesh: Also file a support ticket with NVIDIA — could be kernel ABI change between 535->550 with our specific kernel ABI flags. Will include dmesg + build logs.

kevin: If we drain racks, we lose rack-local aggregation and some jobs will cost more (cross-rack network egress). Estimate: extra networking cost ~ $1.2k/day if we keep racks drained.

jen: Ok, escalation: open a high-priority incident so CS and sales know potential capacity impacts for customers. Tagging #incidents and #support.

sara: Added incident stub, pinged CS. Also started quick AMI rebuild with pinned kernels + kernel-headers for 5.15 and 5.19 variants. ETA for new images ~3h.

matt: One more log snippet (nccl test):
```
NCCL WARN Call to ibv_create_qp failed, errno 22
NCCL INFO P2P send/recv failed between 0<->1
```

kevin: That aligns with NVLINK errors. If modules aren't fully functional GPU DMA and ibverbs path can fail.

jen: Next steps checklist saved in the incident: rollback plan, AMI rebuild, onboarding script change, NVIDIA support ticket, capacity mitigation.

matt: After rollback some jobs still showed longer tails — need to run Optimize to validate batch sizes and latency settings after driver swap.

dinesh: I'll add a unit in our CI that runs DKMS rebuild for latest drivers against all kernels we claim to support. Prevents this from slipping through.

sara: Thanks team. I'll keep updates here. If anyone hits new failing hosts, drop hostnames inline. :thumbsup:

kevin: Filing host list: gpu-usw2-12, gpu-usw2-17, gpu-usw2-23 — draining now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot paused rollout at 40%.

jen: Good. Keep the incident updated. :eyes:"
